body.en: Functions and their graphical representations comprise roughly 15% of the EST I Mathematics exam. Success requires fluency in evaluating composite functions, algebraically constructing and verifying inverse functions, identifying domain restrictions (radicands, denominators), applying transformations (translations, reflections, and vertical/horizontal dilations), and interpreting graph features such as intercepts, maxima/minima, and asymptotes.
body.ar: الدوال and their graphical representations comprise roughly 15% of the EST I Mathematics exam. Success requires fluency in evaluating composite الدوال, algebraically constructing and verifying inverse الدوال, identifying المجال restrictions (radicands, denominators), applying transformations (translations, reflections, and vertical/horizontal dilations), and interpreting التمثيل البياني features such as intercepts, maxima/minima, and خطوط التقارب.

label.en: Definition 3.1 — Function Relations, Domain/Range Restrictions, and Inverses
label.ar: تعريف 3.1 — الدالة Relations, المجال/المدى Restrictions, and Inverses

body.en:
Core definitions and foundational principles of functions:
  • Function Relation & Vertical Line Test: A relation \(f\) from set \(X\) to set \(Y\) is a function if every input \(x \in X\) corresponds to exactly one output \(y \in Y\). Graphically, any vertical line \(x = c\) must intersect the graph at most once.
  • Domain Restrictions: The domain is the set of all real numbers for which the function is defined:
    • Fractions: Denominators cannot equal zero: \(f(x) = \frac{p(x)}{q(x)} \implies q(x) \neq 0\).
    • Even Radicals: Arguments of even roots must be non-negative: \(f(x) = \sqrt{g(x)} \implies g(x) \ge 0\).
    • Logarithms: Arguments must be strictly positive: \(f(x) = \log_b(h(x)) \implies h(x) > 0\).
  • Inverse Functions \(f^{-1}(x)\): If \(f\) is one-to-one (passes the Horizontal Line Test), its inverse \(f^{-1}\) reverses the mapping: \(f(a) = b \iff f^{-1}(b) = a\).
    Graphically, \(y = f^{-1}(x)\) is the reflection of \(y = f(x)\) across the identity line \(y = x\). The domain of \(f\) becomes the range of \(f^{-1}\), and the range of \(f\) becomes the domain of \(f^{-1}\).
  • Fundamental Cancellation Identity:
    \[ (f \circ f^{-1})(x) = f(f^{-1}(x)) = x \quad \text{and} \quad (f^{-1} \circ f)(x) = f^{-1}(f(x)) = x \]
body.ar:
Core definitions and foundational principles of الدوال:
  • Function Relation & Vertical Line Test: A relation \(f\) from set \(X\) to set \(Y\) is a الدالة if every input \(x \in X\) corresponds to exactly one output \(y \in Y\). Graphically, any vertical line \(x = c\) must intersect the التمثيل البياني at most once.
  • Domain Restrictions: The المجال is the set of all real numbers for which the الدالة is defined:
    • Fractions: Denominators cannot equal zero: \(f(x) = \frac{p(x)}{q(x)} \implies q(x) \neq 0\).
    • Even Radicals: Arguments of even roots must be non-negative: \(f(x) = \sqrt{g(x)} \implies g(x) \ge 0\).
    • Logarithms: Arguments must be strictly positive: \(f(x) = \log_b(h(x)) \implies h(x) > 0\).
  • Inverse الدوال \(f^{-1}(x)\): If \(f\) is one-to-one (passes the Horizontal Line Test), its inverse \(f^{-1}\) reverses the mapping: \(f(a) = b \iff f^{-1}(b) = a\).
    Graphically, \(y = f^{-1}(x)\) is the reflection of \(y = f(x)\) across the المتطابقة line \(y = x\). The المجال of \(f\) becomes the المدى of \(f^{-1}\), and the المدى of \(f\) becomes the المجال of \(f^{-1}\).
  • Fundamental Cancellation المتطابقة:
    \[ (f \circ f^{-1})(x) = f(f^{-1}(x)) = x \quad \text{and} \quad (f^{-1} \circ f)(x) = f^{-1}(f(x)) = x \]

body.en: Domain Restrictions, Invertibility & Asymptotic Behavior: An algebraic or transcendental function \(f: D \to R\) possesses an inverse \(f^{-1}: R \to D\) if and only if \(f\) is strictly one-to-one (bijective) on \(D\), guaranteeing that \(\text{dom}(f^{-1}) = \text{ran}(f)\) and \(\text{ran}(f^{-1}) = \text{dom}(f)\). For logarithmic and radical equations, every algebraic step that squares both sides or combines logs (\(\log_b u + \log_b v = \log_b(uv)\)) can enlarge the solution set, requiring a final domain check against the original equation.
body.ar: Domain Restrictions, Invertibility & Asymptotic Behavior: An algebraic or transcendental الدالة \(f: D \to R\) possesses an inverse \(f^{-1}: R \to D\) if and only if \(f\) is strictly one-to-one (bijective) on \(D\), guaranteeing that \(\text{dom}(f^{-1}) = \text{ran}(f)\) and \(\text{ran}(f^{-1}) = \text{dom}(f)\). For logarithmic and radical المعادلات, every algebraic step that squares both sides or combines logs (\(\log_b u + \log_b v = \log_b(uv)\)) can enlarge the الحل set, requiring a final المجال check against the original المعادلة.

label.en: Theorem 3.1 — Function Transformations, Invertibility, and Asymptotic Behavior
label.ar: مبرهنة 3.1 — الدالة Transformations, Invertibility, and Asymptotic Behavior

body.en:
Transformation rules and structural properties for any parent function \(y = f(x)\):
  • Rigid Translations:
    1. \(y = f(x) + k\): Shifts graph vertically up by \(k\) units (down if \(k < 0\)).
    2. \(y = f(x - h)\): Shifts graph horizontally right by \(h\) units (left if \(h < 0\)).
  • Reflections:
    1. \(y = -f(x)\): Reflection across the \(x\)-axis (negates all \(y\)-coordinates).
    2. \(y = f(-x)\): Reflection across the \(y\)-axis (negates all \(x\)-coordinates).
  • Dilations (Stretches & Compressions):
    1. \(y = c \cdot f(x)\) (with \(c > 0\)): Vertical stretch by factor \(c\) if \(c > 1\); vertical compression if \(0 < c < 1\).
    2. \(y = f(c \cdot x)\) (with \(c > 0\)): Horizontal compression by factor \(\frac{1}{c}\) if \(c > 1\); horizontal stretch if \(0 < c < 1\).
  • Rational Function Asymptotes (\(R(x) = \frac{p(x)}{q(x)}\)):
    1. Vertical Asymptotes: Occur at \(x = c\) where \(q(c) = 0\) and \(p(c) \neq 0\).
    2. Horizontal Asymptote: Let \(n = \deg(p)\) and \(m = \deg(q)\):
    • If \(n < m\): Horizontal asymptote at \(y = 0\).
    • If \(n = m\): Horizontal asymptote at \(y = \frac{a_n}{b_m}\) (ratio of leading coefficients).
    • If \(n > m\): No horizontal asymptote (if \(n = m + 1\), an oblique/slant asymptote exists).
body.ar:
Transformation rules and structural properties for any parent الدالة \(y = f(x)\):
  • Rigid Translations:
    1. \(y = f(x) + k\): Shifts التمثيل البياني vertically up by \(k\) units (down if \(k < 0\)).
    2. \(y = f(x - h)\): Shifts التمثيل البياني horizontally right by \(h\) units (left if \(h < 0\)).
  • Reflections:
    1. \(y = -f(x)\): Reflection across the \(x\)-axis (negates all \(y\)-الإحداثيات).
    2. \(y = f(-x)\): Reflection across the \(y\)-axis (negates all \(x\)-الإحداثيات).
  • Dilations (Stretches & Compressions):
    1. \(y = c \cdot f(x)\) (with \(c > 0\)): Vertical stretch by factor \(c\) if \(c > 1\); vertical compression if \(0 < c < 1\).
    2. \(y = f(c \cdot x)\) (with \(c > 0\)): Horizontal compression by factor \(\frac{1}{c}\) if \(c > 1\); horizontal stretch if \(0 < c < 1\).
  • Rational الدالة خطوط التقارب (\(R(x) = \frac{p(x)}{q(x)}\)):
    1. Vertical خطوط التقارب: Occur at \(x = c\) حيث \(q(c) = 0\) and \(p(c) \neq 0\).
    2. Horizontal خط التقارب: Let \(n = \deg(p)\) and \(m = \deg(q)\):
    • If \(n < m\): Horizontal خط التقارب at \(y = 0\).
    • If \(n = m\): Horizontal خط التقارب at \(y = \frac{a_n}{b_m}\) (ratio of leading المعاملات).
    • If \(n > m\): No horizontal خط التقارب (if \(n = m + 1\), an oblique/slant خط التقارب exists).

label.en: ▲ EST I Math Traps & Pitfalls — Functions & Graphs
label.ar: ▲ EST I Math Traps & Pitfalls — الدوال & Graphs

body.en:
• Horizontal Shift Reversal: The transformation \(f(x - h)\) shifts the graph to the RIGHT by \(h\), while \(f(x + h)\) shifts the graph to the LEFT by \(h\). The sign inside the parentheses always behaves counter-intuitively.
  • Composition Evaluation Order: For \((f \circ g)(x) = f(g(x))\), always calculate the inner function \(g(x)\) first, then feed the result into the outer function \(f\). In general, \(f(g(x)) \neq g(f(x))\).
  • Inverse vs. Reciprocal: Do not confuse the inverse function \(f^{-1}(x)\) with the multiplicative reciprocal \([f(x)]^{-1} = \frac{1}{f(x)}\). They are completely distinct concepts.
  • Removable Discontinuities (Holes) vs. Vertical Asymptotes: If a common factor cancels in a rational function, such as \(\frac{(x - 3)(x + 2)}{x - 3} = x + 2\), there is a hole at \(x = 3\) (coordinates \((3, 5)\)), NOT a vertical asymptote!
body.ar:
• Horizontal Shift Reversal: The transformation \(f(x - h)\) shifts the التمثيل البياني to the RIGHT by \(h\), while \(f(x + h)\) shifts the التمثيل البياني to the LEFT by \(h\). The sign inside the parentheses always behaves counter-intuitively.
  • Composition Evaluation Order: For \((f \circ g)(x) = f(g(x))\), always احسب inner الدالة \(g(x)\) first, then feed the result into the outer الدالة \(f\). In general, \(f(g(x)) \neq g(f(x))\).
  • Inverse vs. Reciprocal: Do not confuse the inverse الدالة \(f^{-1}(x)\) with the multiplicative reciprocal \([f(x)]^{-1} = \frac{1}{f(x)}\). They are completely distinct concepts.
  • Removable Discontinuities (Holes) vs. Vertical خطوط التقارب: If a common factor cancels in a rational الدالة, such as \(\frac{(x - 3)(x + 2)}{x - 3} = x + 2\), there is a hole at \(x = 3\) (الإحداثيات \((3, 5)\)), NOT a vertical خط التقارب!

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Functions & Graphs)
label.ar: ◆ لماذا تعمل هذه الطريقة رياضياً — First-Principles اشتقاق (الدوال & Graphs)

body.en:
Why Completing the Square & Log-Linearization Work: Any quadratic \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) (\(a \ne 0\)) can be rewritten by factoring \(a\) from the first two terms and adding/subtracting \((b/2a)^2\):

\[ ax^2 + bx + c = a\!\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 + \left(c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\right) \]

Because \(\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 \ge 0\) for all \(x \in \mathbb{R}\), the extreme value \(k = c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\) is attained uniquely at the axis of symmetry \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\), restricting the range to \([k, \infty)\) (if \(a > 0\)) and making \(f\) invertible on \(x \ge -\frac{b}{2a}\). Similarly, applying \(\ln\) to power laws \(y = ax^n\) yields \(\ln y = n\ln x + \ln a\), transforming a nonlinear curve into a straight line of gradient \(n\).

\[ ax^2 + bx + c = a\!\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 + \left(c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\right) \]

Because \(\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 \ge 0\) for all \(x \in \mathbb{R}\), the extreme value \(k = c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\) is attained uniquely at the axis of symmetry \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\), restricting the المدى to \([k, \infty)\) (if \(a > 0\)) and making \(f\) invertible on \(x \ge -\frac{b}{2a}\). Similarly, applying \(\ln\) to power laws \(y = ax^n\) yields \(\ln y = n\ln x + \ln a\), transforming a nonlinear curve into a straight line of gradient \(n\).

label.en: Worked Example 3.A — Multi-Level Function Composition & Evaluation
label.ar: مثال محلول 3.A — Multi-Level الدالة Composition & Evaluation

body.en:
Let \(f(x) = 2x^2 - 3x + 1\) and \(g(x) = 3x - 5\).
(a) Evaluate \(f(g(2))\).
(b) Evaluate \(g(f(-1))\).
(c) Find all real values of \(x\) such that \((g \circ f)(x) = 1\).

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. (a) Evaluate \(f(g(2))\):
    First evaluate the inner function: \[ g(2) = 3(2) - 5 = 6 - 5 = 1 \]
    Now evaluate \(f(1)\): \[ f(1) = 2(1)^2 - 3(1) + 1 = 2 - 3 + 1 = \mathbf{0} \]
  2. (b) Evaluate \(g(f(-1))\):
    Evaluate the inner function: \[ f(-1) = 2(-1)^2 - 3(-1) + 1 = 2(1) + 3 + 1 = 6 \]
    Now evaluate \(g(6)\): \[ g(6) = 3(6) - 5 = 18 - 5 = \mathbf{13} \]
  3. (c) Solve \(g(f(x)) = 1\):
    Substitute \(f(x)\) into \(g\): \[ g(f(x)) = 3(2x^2 - 3x + 1) - 5 = 6x^2 - 9x + 3 - 5 = 6x^2 - 9x - 2 \]
    Set equal to 1: \[ 6x^2 - 9x - 2 = 1 \implies 6x^2 - 9x - 3 = 0 \implies 2x^2 - 3x - 1 = 0 \]
    Using the quadratic formula: \[ x = \frac{-(-3) \pm \sqrt{(-3)^2 - 4(2)(-1)}}{2(2)} = \mathbf{\frac{3 \pm \sqrt{17}}{4}} \]
body.ar:
Let \(f(x) = 2x^2 - 3x + 1\) and \(g(x) = 3x - 5\).
(a) احسب قيمة \(f(g(2))\).
(b) احسب قيمة \(g(f(-1))\).
(c) Find all real values of \(x\) such that \((g \circ f)(x) = 1\).

Step-by-step الحل:
  1. (a) احسب قيمة \(f(g(2))\):
    First احسب قيمة inner الدالة: \[ g(2) = 3(2) - 5 = 6 - 5 = 1 \]
    Now احسب قيمة \(f(1)\): \[ f(1) = 2(1)^2 - 3(1) + 1 = 2 - 3 + 1 = \mathbf{0} \]
  2. (b) احسب قيمة \(g(f(-1))\):
    Evaluate the inner الدالة: \[ f(-1) = 2(-1)^2 - 3(-1) + 1 = 2(1) + 3 + 1 = 6 \]
    Now احسب قيمة \(g(6)\): \[ g(6) = 3(6) - 5 = 18 - 5 = \mathbf{13} \]
  3. (c) Solve \(g(f(x)) = 1\):
    Substitute \(f(x)\) into \(g\): \[ g(f(x)) = 3(2x^2 - 3x + 1) - 5 = 6x^2 - 9x + 3 - 5 = 6x^2 - 9x - 2 \]
    Set equal to 1: \[ 6x^2 - 9x - 2 = 1 \implies 6x^2 - 9x - 3 = 0 \implies 2x^2 - 3x - 1 = 0 \]
    Using the quadratic الصيغة: \[ x = \frac{-(-3) \pm \sqrt{(-3)^2 - 4(2)(-1)}}{2(2)} = \mathbf{\frac{3 \pm \sqrt{17}}{4}} \]

label.en: Worked Example 3.B — Algebraic Construction of Inverse Functions
label.ar: مثال محلول 3.B — Algebraic Construction of Inverse الدوال

body.en:
Consider the one-to-one rational function \(f(x) = \dfrac{4x + 3}{2x - 5}\) for \(x eq rac{5}{2}\).
(a) Find an explicit expression for \(f^{-1}(x)\).
(b) State the domain and range of \(f^{-1}(x)\).
(c) Verify that \(f^{-1}(f(4)) = 4\).

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. (a) Construct \(f^{-1}(x)\):
    Set \(y = rac{4x + 3}{2x - 5}\), then swap \(x\) and \(y\):
    \[ x = rac{4y + 3}{2y - 5} \]
    Multiply both sides by \((2y - 5)\):
    \[ x(2y - 5) = 4y + 3 \implies 2xy - 5x = 4y + 3 \]
    Group all terms containing \(y\) on one side:
    \[ 2xy - 4y = 5x + 3 \implies y(2x - 4) = 5x + 3 \implies y = rac{5x + 3}{2x - 4} \]
    Therefore, \(f^{-1}(x) = \mathbf{\dfrac{5x + 3}{2x - 4}}\).
  2. (b) Domain and Range:
    The denominator cannot equal zero: \(2x - 4 eq 0 \implies x eq 2\).
    Domain of \(f^{-1}\): \(\mathbf{(-\infty, 2) \cup (2, \infty)}\).
    Range of \(f^{-1}\) is the domain of \(f\): \(\mathbf{(-\infty, 2.5) \cup (2.5, \infty)}\).
  3. (c) Verification:
    \[ f(4) = rac{4(4) + 3}{2(4) - 5} = rac{16 + 3}{8 - 5} = rac{19}{3} \]
    \[ f^{-1}\left( rac{19}{3} ight) = rac{5\left( rac{19}{3} ight) + 3}{2\left( rac{19}{3} ight) - 4} = rac{ rac{95 + 9}{3}}{ rac{38 - 12}{3}} = rac{104}{26} = \mathbf{4} \quad \checkmark \]
body.ar:
Consider the one-to-one rational الدالة \(f(x) = \dfrac{4x + 3}{2x - 5}\) for \(x eq rac{5}{2}\).
(a) Find an explicit العبارة الجبرية for \(f^{-1}(x)\).
(b) State the المجال and المدى of \(f^{-1}(x)\).
(c) Verify that \(f^{-1}(f(4)) = 4\).

Step-by-step الحل:
  1. (a) Construct \(f^{-1}(x)\):
    Set \(y = rac{4x + 3}{2x - 5}\), then swap \(x\) and \(y\):
    \[ x = rac{4y + 3}{2y - 5} \]
    Multiply both sides by \((2y - 5)\):
    \[ x(2y - 5) = 4y + 3 \implies 2xy - 5x = 4y + 3 \]
    Group all terms containing \(y\) on one side:
    \[ 2xy - 4y = 5x + 3 \implies y(2x - 4) = 5x + 3 \implies y = rac{5x + 3}{2x - 4} \]
    Therefore, \(f^{-1}(x) = \mathbf{\dfrac{5x + 3}{2x - 4}}\).
  2. (b) المجال and المدى:
    The denominator cannot equal zero: \(2x - 4 eq 0 \implies x eq 2\).
    Domain of \(f^{-1}\): \(\mathbf{(-\infty, 2) \cup (2, \infty)}\).
    Range of \(f^{-1}\) is the المجال of \(f\): \(\mathbf{(-\infty, 2.5) \cup (2.5, \infty)}\).
  3. (c) Verification:
    \[ f(4) = rac{4(4) + 3}{2(4) - 5} = rac{16 + 3}{8 - 5} = rac{19}{3} \]
    \[ f^{-1}\left( rac{19}{3} ight) = rac{5\left( rac{19}{3} ight) + 3}{2\left( rac{19}{3} ight) - 4} = rac{ rac{95 + 9}{3}}{ rac{38 - 12}{3}} = rac{104}{26} = \mathbf{4} \quad \checkmark \]

label.ar: مثال محلول 3.C — Multi-Step التمثيل البياني Transformations

body.en:
The function \(g(x)\) is defined by transforming \(f(x)\) according to \(g(x) = -2f(x + 4) - 3\).
(a) List the sequence of elementary transformations that maps the graph of \(f(x)\) onto \(g(x)\).
(b) If the point \((2, 5)\) lies on the graph of \(y = f(x)\), determine the coordinates of the corresponding point on the graph of \(y = g(x)\).

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. (a) Transformation Sequence:
    1. Horizontal translation: Shift left by 4 units (\(x \to x - 4\)).
    2. Vertical dilation: Vertical stretch by a factor of 2.
    3. Reflection: Reflect across the \(x\)-axis (multiply \(y\) by \(-1\)).
    4. Vertical translation: Shift downward by 3 units (subtract 3 from \(y\)).
  2. (b) Point Mapping:
    Apply coordinate mapping \((x, y) \to (x - 4, -2y - 3)\):
    New \(x\)-coordinate: \(x' = 2 - 4 = -2\)
    New \(y\)-coordinate: \(y' = -2(5) - 3 = -10 - 3 = -13\)
    The mapped point is \(\mathbf{(-2, -13)}\).
body.ar:
The الدالة \(g(x)\) is defined by transforming \(f(x)\) according to \(g(x) = -2f(x + 4) - 3\).
(a) List the المتتالية of elementary transformations that maps the التمثيل البياني of \(f(x)\) onto \(g(x)\).
(b) If the point \((2, 5)\) lies on the التمثيل البياني of \(y = f(x)\), حدّد الإحداثيات of the corresponding point on the التمثيل البياني of \(y = g(x)\).

Step-by-step الحل:
  1. (a) Transformation المتتالية:
    1. Horizontal translation: Shift left by 4 units (\(x \to x - 4\)).
    2. Vertical dilation: Vertical stretch by a factor of 2.
    3. Reflection: Reflect across the \(x\)-axis (multiply \(y\) by \(-1\)).
    4. Vertical translation: Shift downward by 3 units (subtract 3 from \(y\)).
  2. (b) Point Mapping:
    Apply الإحداثي mapping \((x, y) \to (x - 4, -2y - 3)\):
    New \(x\)-الإحداثي: \(x' = 2 - 4 = -2\)
    New \(y\)-الإحداثي: \(y' = -2(5) - 3 = -10 - 3 = -13\)
    The mapped point is \(\mathbf{(-2, -13)}\).

body.en:
Problem (Easy): The graph of the quadratic function \( f(x) = x^2 - 4x + 3 \) is shown below. What is the value of \( f(0) \)?

Step-by-Step Solution: To find the value of \( f(0) \), we substitute \( x = 0 \) into the function's equation: \( f(x) = x^2 - 4x + 3 \). Therefore, \( f(0) = (0)^2 - 4(0) + 3 = 0 - 0 + 3 = 3 \). This corresponds to the y-intercept of the graph.
body.ar:
Problem (Easy): The التمثيل البياني of the quadratic الدالة \( f(x) = x^2 - 4x + 3 \) is shown below. What is the value of \( f(0) \)?

Step-by-Step الحل: To أوجد قيمة \( f(0) \), we عوّض \( x = 0 \) into the الدالة's المعادلة: \( f(x) = x^2 - 4x + 3 \). وبالتالي, \( f(0) = (0)^2 - 4(0) + 3 = 0 - 0 + 3 = 3 \). This corresponds to the y-المقطع of the التمثيل البياني.

question.en: Determine the maximal real domain of the function \(f(x) = \dfrac{\sqrt{3x - 12}}{x^2 - 25}\). Express your answer in interval notation.
question.ar: حدّد maximal real domain of the function \(f(x) = \dfrac{\sqrt{3x - 12}}{x^2 - 25}\). Express your answer in interval notation.

solution.en:
Step 1: For the square root in the numerator to be defined over the reals, the radicand must be non-negative: \[ 3x - 12 \ge 0 \implies 3x \ge 12 \implies x \ge 4. \]

Step 2: For the denominator to be non-zero: \[ x^2 - 25 eq 0 \implies x eq 5 \quad \text{and} \quad x eq -5. \]

Step 3: Intersect the conditions \(x \ge 4\) and \(x eq 5\) (note that \(x = -5\) is already outside \(x \ge 4\)): \[ [4, 5) \cup (5, \infty). \]

The maximal real domain is \(\mathbf{[4, 5) \cup (5, \infty)}\).

question.en: Let \(f(x) = \dfrac{2x - 7}{5}\). (a) Find \(f^{-1}(x)\). (b) Solve the equation \(f(f^{-1}(x)) = 9\). (c) Find the value of \(k\) for which \(f(k) = f^{-1}(k)\).
question.ar: ليكن \(f(x) = \dfrac{2x - 7}{5}\). (a) أوجد \(f^{-1}(x)\). (b) حل المعادلة \(f(f^{-1}(x)) = 9\). (c) أوجد قيمة \(k\) for which \(f(k) = f^{-1}(k)\).

solution.en:
(a) Find \(f^{-1}(x)\): Let \(y = \frac{2x - 7}{5}\). Swap \(x\) and \(y\): \[ x = \frac{2y - 7}{5} \implies 5x = 2y - 7 \implies 2y = 5x + 7 \implies \mathbf{f^{-1}(x) = \frac{5x + 7}{2}}. \]

(b) Composition identity: By definition, for all \(x\) in the domain of \(f^{-1}\), \(f(f^{-1}(x)) = x\). Therefore, \(f(f^{-1}(x)) = 9 \implies \mathbf{x = 9}\).

(c) Point on line \(y = x\): If \(f(k) = f^{-1}(k)\), the intersection must lie on the line of reflection \(y = x\). Setting \(f(k) = k\): \[ \frac{2k - 7}{5} = k \implies 2k - 7 = 5k \implies 3k = -7 \implies \mathbf{k = -\frac{7}{3}}. \]

question.en: Given \(f(x) = x^2 - 4x + 7\) with restricted domain \(x \ge 2\), find an explicit formula for \(f^{-1}(x)\) and state its domain.
question.ar: Given \(f(x) = x^2 - 4x + 7\) with restricted domain \(x \ge 2\), أوجد an explicit formula for \(f^{-1}(x)\) and state its domain.

solution.en:
Step 1: Complete the square to isolate \(x\): \[ y = (x^2 - 4x + 4) + 3 = (x - 2)^2 + 3. \]

Step 2: Swap \(x\) and \(y\) (with \(y \ge 2\)): \[ x = (y - 2)^2 + 3 \implies (y - 2)^2 = x - 3. \]

Step 3: Take the principal square root (since \(y \ge 2 \implies y - 2 \ge 0\)): \[ y - 2 = +\sqrt{x - 3} \implies y = 2 + \sqrt{x - 3}. \]

Therefore, \(\mathbf{f^{-1}(x) = 2 + \sqrt{x - 3}}\), defined for domain \(\mathbf{x \ge 3}\) (which matches the range of \(f\)).

question.en: The graph of \(y = f(x)\) passes through the points \((-2, 8)\) and \((4, -6)\). If \(g(x) = 3f(x - 5) + 2\), determine the corresponding points on the graph of \(g(x)\).
question.ar: The graph of \(y = f(x)\) يمر بالنقطة the points \((-2, 8)\) and \((4, -6)\). إذا كان \(g(x) = 3f(x - 5) + 2\), حدّد corresponding points on the graph of \(g(x)\).

solution.en:
Transformation Mapping: For any point \((x, y)\) on \(f\), the corresponding point on \(g(x) = 3f(x - 5) + 2\) has coordinates: \[ (x', y') = (x + 5, 3y + 2). \]

For point 1: \((-2, 8)\): \[ x'_1 = -2 + 5 = 3, \qquad y'_1 = 3(8) + 2 = 24 + 2 = 26 \implies \mathbf{(3, 26)}. \]

For point 2: \((4, -6)\): \[ x'_2 = 4 + 5 = 9, \qquad y'_2 = 3(-6) + 2 = -18 + 2 = -16 \implies \mathbf{(9, -16)}. \]

The corresponding points on \(g(x)\) are \(\mathbf{(3, 26)}\) and \(\mathbf{(9, -16)}\).

question.en: Consider the function \(f(x)\) defined by \(f(x) = |x-2| + |x+1|\). Find the minimum value of \(f(x)\) and the interval over which this minimum is attained.
question.ar: Consider the function \(f(x)\) defined by \(f(x) = |x-2| + |x+1|\). أوجد minimum value of \(f(x)\) and the interval over which this minimum is attained.

hints.en: The function is defined as \(f(x) = |x-2| + |x+1|\). We can analyze this function by considering the critical points where the expressions inside the absolute values change sign, which are \(x=2\) and \(x=-1\). This divides the number line into three intervals: Case 1: \(x < -1\).
hints.ar: The function is defined as \(f(x) = |x-2| + |x+1|\). We can analyze this function by considering the critical points حيث the expressions inside the absolute values change sign, which are \(x=2\) and \(x=-1\). This divides the number line into three intervals: Case 1: \(x < -1\).

hints.en: In this interval, \((x-2)\) is negative and \((x+1)\) is negative. So, \(f(x) = -(x-2) - (x+1) = -x+2 -x-1 = -2x+1\). This is a decreasing linear function. Case 2: \(-1 \le x \le 2\).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \((x-2)\) ، \((x+1)\) ، \(f(x) = -(x-2) - (x+1) = -x+2 -x-1 = -2x+1\) ، \(-1 \le x \le 2\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

hints.en: Therefore, the minimum value of \(f(x)\) is 3, and this minimum value is attained for all \(x\) in the interval \([-1, 2]\).
hints.ar: وبالتالي، the minimum value of \(f(x)\) is 3, and this minimum value is attained for all \(x\) in the interval \([-1, 2]\).

solution.en:
The function is defined as \(f(x) = |x-2| + |x+1|\). We can analyze this function by considering the critical points where the expressions inside the absolute values change sign, which are \(x=2\) and \(x=-1\). This divides the number line into three intervals:

Case 1: \(x < -1\)
In this interval, \((x-2)\) is negative and \((x+1)\) is negative. So, \(f(x) = -(x-2) - (x+1) = -x+2 -x-1 = -2x+1\). This is a decreasing linear function.

Case 2: \(-1 \le x \le 2\)
In this interval, \((x-2)\) is non-positive and \((x+1)\) is non-negative. So, \(f(x) = -(x-2) + (x+1) = -x+2 +x+1 = 3\). This is a constant function.

Case 3: \(x > 2\)
In this interval, \((x-2)\) is positive and \((x+1)\) is positive. So, \(f(x) = (x-2) + (x+1) = x-2 +x+1 = 2x-1\). This is an increasing linear function.

Combining these cases, we see that:
- For \(x < -1\), \(f(x)\) decreases.
- For \(-1 \le x \le 2\), \(f(x) = 3\).
- For \(x > 2\), \(f(x)\) increases.

Therefore, the minimum value of \(f(x)\) is 3, and this minimum value is attained for all \(x\) in the interval \([-1, 2]\).

Common misconception: Students might incorrectly assume the minimum occurs at one of the critical points and not consider the interval where the function is constant. For example, if they only check \(x=-1\), they might get \(f(-1) = |-1-2| + |-1+1| = |-3| + |0| = 3\). If they only check \(x=2\), they might get \(f(2) = |2-2| + |2+1| = |0| + |3| = 3\). However, they must also confirm that the function does not dip below 3 in any other interval. The analysis of the three cases shows this is indeed the minimum.

label.en: ● Master Atlas of the 9 Main Parent Functions & Universal Transformation Law
label.ar: ● الأطلس الشامل للدوال الأم التسع وقانون التحويلات الهندسية العام

body.en:
Every algebraic and elementary transcendental model is built by transforming one of the nine core parent functions via \(g(x) = a\,f(x - h) + k\), where \(|a|\) scales vertically (reflecting across the \(x\)-axis if \(a < 0\)), \(h\) shifts horizontally, and \(k\) shifts vertically:

FamilyTransformed Form \(g(x)\)DomainRange (\(a > 0\))Key Geometric Feature
Constant\(f(x) = c\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\{c\}\)Horizontal line, slope \(0\)
Linear\(a(x - h) + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)Constant slope \(m = a\), pivot \((h, k)\)
Quadratic\(a(x - h)^2 + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)Parabola vertex \((h, k)\), axis \(x = h\)
Cubic\(a(x - h)^3 + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)Inflection center \((h, k)\), S-curve
Absolute Value\(a|x - h| + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)V-corner vertex \((h, k)\), slopes \(\pm a\)
Radical\(a\sqrt{x - h} + k\)\([h, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)Endpoint \((h, k)\), half-parabola
Rational\(\dfrac{a}{x - h} + k\)\(x \neq h\)\(y \neq k\)Vertical asymptote \(x = h\), horizontal \(y = k\)
Exponential\(a \cdot 2^{x - h} + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((k, \infty)\)Horizontal asymptote \(y = k\), anchor \((h, a+k)\)
Logarithmic\(a\ln(x - h) + k\)\((h, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)Vertical asymptote \(x = h\), anchor \((h+1, k)\)
body.ar:

عائلة الدالةالصورة المحوّلة \(g(x)\)المجالالمدى (\(a > 0\))السمة الهندسية المميزة

note.en: Starts on the absolute value (modulus) family \(f(x) = a|x - h| + k\) with V-vertex \((h, k)\) and symmetric branch slopes \(\pm a\). Drag \((h, k)\) or switch between all 9 parent functions.
note.ar: يبدأ على دالة القيمة المطلقة \(f(x) = a|x - h| + k\) ذات الرأس \((h, k)\) وفرعي الميل المتناظرين \(\pm a\). اسحب \((h, k)\) أو بدّل بين الدوال الأم التسع.
